title: The Timing of the Middle Pleistocene Glacial Terminations Based on 40Ar/39Ar Detrital Sanidine Dating
content:
Abstract

Sediments were deposited since 1,300 ka in the Paleotiber delta, near the coast of Rome. They generally consist of fining-upward sequences, with abrupt transitions from gravel to sand and/or clay that reflect changes in the regional base level due to rapid sea-level rise. These aggradational successions can be precisely dated using 40Ar/39Ar geochronology, by exploiting the frequent volcanic activity of the Roman Magmatic Region and the associated widespread occurrence of potassium-rich primary volcanic deposits. Here we present, new detrital sanidine 40Ar/39Ar-based chronologies for five aggradational successions deposited between ∼960 ka and ∼600 ka in the Paleotiber delta that are corroborated by vertical and lateral stratigraphic analysis. This stratigraphic framework of fining-upward sequences is interpreted as the local expression of high-amplitude, sea-level rise during the glacial terminations of the Middle Pleistocene. Comparison with a global stack of stable oxygen isotopes measured in benthic foraminifera and/or with radiometrically dated speleothems shows agreement across glacial terminations XII, IX, and VIII, while a ∼10 kyr mismatch is found in the timing of glacial termination VII. The relatively small chronological uncertainties (2–2.5 kyr at the 2σ level) associated with the reconstructed timing of glacial termination IX allow for a direct comparison with the last glacial termination, revealing remarkably similar lags behind orbital forcing, as both terminations share a similar orbital configuration but differ in the ice volumes at their preceding glacial maxima.
